title: Work-cell update rule
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, and let $w$ be a binary input. Fix a time $t\in\mathbb N$, a work tape $\tau$, a cell position $z\in\mathbb Z$, and a finite list of bits $l$. Suppose the first bit of $l$ is false, its snapshot field decodes to the machine's snapshot on $w$ at time $t$, and its designated neighboring-head bits record whether the tape head at time $t$ is at $z-1$, $z$, and $z+1$. Suppose also that the designated content bits record whether cell $z$ contains a bit and, if so, its value; and that the designated chain bits record whether the time-$t+1$ work-chain value at $z-1$ exists and, if so, its value. Then the local work-cell update rule applied to $l$ yields the encoding of the time-$t+1$ head indicator, cell content, and work-chain value at $z$.
hypotheses_covered: decoded prior snapshot equals the run snapshot at time t
neighboring-head bits encode head positions z−1, z, z+1
cell-content presence and value bits encode cell z at time t
chain presence and value bits encode the time-(t+1) chain at z−1
